input: Find fraud and bribery allegations involving Adani Green Energy, including the US indictment

entity.group: Adani Group (majority-owned by the Adani family; TotalEnergies holds a minority stake)
entity.hq_country: India (registered office: Adani Corporate House, Shantigram, S G Highway, Khodiyar, Ahmedabad - 382 421, Gujarat, India; CIN L40106GJ2015PLC082007)
entity.legal_name: Adani Green Energy Limited (AGEL), listed on BSE and NSE with effect from June 18, 2018

events.date: Filed under seal October 24, 2024; unsealed November 20, 2024; dismissed with prejudice by court order dated August 10, 2026
events.type: Bribery / foreign bribery (FCPA conspiracy), securities fraud conspiracy, wire fraud conspiracy, securities fraud, and conspiracy to obstruct justice - US criminal indictment
events.amount: Approximately $265 million in bribes to Indian government officials for lucrative solar energy supply contracts; billions of dollars (over $3 billion per the indictment's financing allegations) raised from US investors and international financial institutions
events.status: Charged 2024; on May 18, 2026 the DOJ moved under Rule 48(a) to dismiss with prejudice, and on August 10, 2026 the EDNY court dismissed the indictment against Gautam S. Adani, Sagar R. Adani and Vneet S. Jaain with prejudice; judgment was reserved on Counts One and Five (FCPA and obstruction) as to the non-appearing defendants (Gupta, Cabanes, Saurabh Agarwal, Malhotra, Rupesh Agarwal) pending DOJ fulfillment of Rule 48(a) requirements; arrest warrants remain outstanding
events.parties: United States v. Gautam S. Adani (Chairman, Adani Green), Sagar R. Adani (Executive Director, Adani Green), Vneet S. Jaain (Managing Director, Adani Green), plus Ranjit Gupta, Cyril Cabanes, Saurabh Agarwal, Deepak Malhotra and Rupesh Agarwal (Azure Power/CDPQ-linked individuals); Adani Green Energy Limited itself was not a defendant and no charges were brought against the company
events.summary: Five-count US DOJ indictment (US v. Gautam S. Adani et al., No. 24-CR-433, E.D.N.Y., Judge Nicholas G. Garaufis; USAO #2022R00935) alleging a 2020-2024 scheme by Adani Green's senior executives to pay approximately $265 million in bribes to Indian state government officials to secure solar energy supply contracts and to misrepresent Adani Green's anti-bribery practices to US investors and international financial institutions to obtain billions of dollars in financing.
events.jurisdiction: United States - US District Court for the Eastern District of New York (Brooklyn)

events.date: Charged November 20, 2024; SEC moved for final judgments by consent on May 14, 2026
events.type: Securities fraud (SEC civil enforcement) - false statements about anti-bribery compliance in Adani Green's September 2021 $750 million bond offering, which raised more than $175 million from US investors
events.amount: Alleged bribes of the equivalent of hundreds of millions of dollars; $750 million bond offering (>$175 million from US investors); proposed civil penalties of $6,000,000 (Gautam Adani) and $12,000,000 (Sagar Adani)
events.status: Charged (SEC v. Gautam Adani and Sagar Adani, No. 1:24-cv-08080, E.D.N.Y., under Securities Act Section 17(a) and Exchange Act Section 10(b)/Rule 10b-5); settled - without admitting or denying the allegations, both defendants consented to permanent injunctions and civil monetary penalties of $6,000,000 and $12,000,000 respectively, subject to court approval
events.parties: Gautam Adani (founder/Chairman of Adani Green's Board) and Sagar Adani (Executive Director of Adani Green's Board); SEC complaint also names the conduct as benefiting Adani Green Energy Ltd.
events.summary: The SEC alleged that Gautam and Sagar Adani orchestrated a bribery scheme paying or promising hundreds of millions of dollars in bribes to Indian government officials for above-market energy purchase commitments benefiting Adani Green, and that during a September 2021 $750 million note offering they falsely touted Adani Green's anti-corruption and anti-bribery compliance.
events.jurisdiction: United States - US District Court for the Eastern District of New York (SEC administrative/civil)

events.type: Foreign bribery (FCPA) - SEC civil enforcement against a participant in the same alleged bribery scheme
events.status: Charged (SEC v. Cyril Sebastien Dominique Cabanes, No. 1:24-cv-08081, E.D.N.Y.); alleged; seeks permanent injunction, civil penalty and officer-and-director bar
events.parties: Cyril Cabanes, former member of Azure Power's Board of Directors - included because the alleged bribery scheme's purpose was to secure above-market energy purchase commitments benefiting Adani Green and Azure Power
events.summary: Parallel SEC action charging Cabanes with FCPA violations for allegedly facilitating the authorization of bribes in furtherance of the same scheme that benefited Adani Green, the first SEC FCPA individual enforcement action since October 2020.
events.jurisdiction: United States - US District Court for the Eastern District of New York

events.date: Report published January 24, 2023; SEBI dismissed key allegations September 2025
events.type: Short-seller fraud allegations (accounting irregularities, stock manipulation, use of offshore shell entities) and resulting regulatory investigation - group-wide, including Adani Green Energy
events.amount: Adani Green Energy stock fell approximately 43% to roughly INR 765 by February 2, 2023 after the report; the group lost more than $100 billion in market value in days
events.status: Alleged; SEBI investigated from 2023; in September 2025 SEBI dismissed the allegations against Adani companies, holding the inquiry revealed no violation of regulatory norms (no manipulative or fraudulent transactions), while 22 other SEBI cases on issues from insider trading to public float violations remained pending per Reuters
events.parties: Hindenburg Research (short-seller) vs Adani Group companies including Adani Green Energy; Hindenburg founder Nate Anderson disbanded the firm in 2025
events.summary: Hindenburg Research's 106-page report accused the Adani Group of accounting irregularities, stock price manipulation and using offshore shell entities; Adani Green shares lost about 43% of their value, and SEBI's subsequent investigation concluded in September 2025 with the allegations dismissed as baseless (two charges cleared, others pending).

events.date: SCN dated November 10, 2023; investigation period January 28, 2021 to August 20, 2021; SEBI order December 2025
events.type: Insider trading in the scrip of Adani Green Energy Limited - trading on unpublished price sensitive information (UPSI)
events.amount: Alleged unlawful profit of INR 3,51,37,030.8 in total (INR 1,42,19,866.3 by Noticee No. 2, INR 1,56,09,149 by Noticee No. 3, INR 53,08,015.5 by Noticee No. 4); 2 lakh shares bought during the UPSI period were 29.36% of the day's volume on NSE; entire holding sold for INR 25.05 crore post-UPSI
events.status: Alleged - SEBI adjudication ongoing; settlement applications by the noticees were disposed of as withdrawn (Noticee No. 1 on June 23, 2025; Noticees No. 2, 3 and 4 on September 26, 2025)
events.parties: Vinod Bahety (Adani Group Head of M&A from February 2021; alleged communication of UPSI), Tarun Jain, M/s Rajtaru Enterprises, and MC Jain Infosystems Pvt Ltd; UPSI concerned Adani Green's May 19, 2021 acquisition of SB Energy from Softbank Group Capital and Bharti Global
events.summary: SEBI order in the matter of alleged insider trading in Adani Green Energy Limited's shares ahead of the announcement of AGEL's acquisition of SB Energy on May 19, 2021, alleging that the Adani Group's head of M&A communicated UPSI and that connected entities traded on it for unlawful profits of about INR 3.51 crore.

events.date: DOJ Rule 48(a) motion filed May 18, 2026; Senators Warren and Blumenthal letter to Acting AG Todd Blanche dated June 11, 2026
events.type: Government-inquiry / oversight - US Senators' inquiry into the DOJ's withdrawal of the Adani prosecution and an alleged quid-pro-quo
events.amount: Reported $10 billion US investment offer by Adani, made in April 2026 after Adani hired Trump's personal lawyer Robert J. Giuffra Jr.
events.status: Investigation ongoing - the letter questions the DOJ's dropping of the prosecution; the underlying DOJ criminal charges were dismissed with prejudice on August 10, 2026 as to the three Adani Green directors
events.parties: US Senators Elizabeth Warren and Richard Blumenthal vs US DOJ (Acting AG Todd Blanche) regarding the prosecution of Gautam Adani and co-defendants
events.summary: Senators Warren and Blumenthal wrote to the Acting Attorney General questioning the DOJ's motion to dismiss the Adani indictment with prejudice, reportedly made after Adani hired former Trump lawyer Robert J. Giuffra Jr., who offered a $10 billion US investment, and describing the indictment as a 'name and shame' case brought without realistic prospect of trial per the DOJ's stated rationale.
events.jurisdiction: United States (Congressional oversight of DOJ; underlying case E.D.N.Y.)

output.assessment: As of November 2026, Adani Green Energy's principal exposure is the US EDNY criminal indictment (No. 24-CR-433) alleging ~$265 million in bribes to Indian state officials and securities fraud in its $750 million 2021 US bond offering - but the DOJ dismissed the charges against its directors with prejudice on August 10, 2026, and the SEC's parallel civil case was settled by consent ($6 million Gautam Adani, $12 million Sagar Adani, no admission of wrongdoing, subject to court approval). Residual open risk includes the reserved judgment on the FCPA and obstruction counts against the non-appearing defendants (Gupta, Cabanes, S. Agarwal, Malhotra, R. Agarwal), whose arrest warrants remain outstanding; the pending court approval of the SEC consent judgments; a June 2026 Senate inquiry into the circumstances of the DOJ's dismissal; and SEBI's still-pending insider trading adjudication in Adani Green's scrip. SEBI dismissed the Hindenburg allegations in September 2025, removing one overhang, though 22 related SEBI cases reportedly remained pending.
missing_fields: Court approval status of the SEC's May 14, 2026 consent final judgments (Gautam Adani $6M / Sagar Adani $12M) as of today - the release states the judgments were only 'subject to court approval'
Final outcome of the reserved judgment on Counts One and Five (FCPA and obstruction conspiracy) against the non-appearing defendants
Outcome of the remaining 22 pending SEBI cases (insider trading to public float violations) as they may affect Adani Green Energy specifically

excluded_namesakes.name: Azure Power Global Limited (Mauritius-incorporated, formerly NYSE-listed)
excluded_namesakes.reason: Azure Power and its former executives (Ranjit Gupta, Cyril Cabanes, Saurabh Agarwal, Deepak Malhotra, Rupesh Agarwal) were charged in the same alleged bribery scheme, but it is a distinct company from Adani Green Energy - excluded as the subject entity; only Adani Green executives' role is in scope.

excluded_namesakes.name: Adani Enterprises Limited
excluded_namesakes.reason: Adani Enterprises (a separate Adani group company, not Adani Green Energy) was the entity in the reported May 18, 2026 US Treasury/OFAC settlement (~$275 million per Reuters) over alleged Iran-origin LPG shipments - a sanctions matter that does not attach to Adani Green Energy, so it is excluded from its events.

excluded_namesakes.name: Adani Enterprises Ltd, Adani Power Ltd, Adani Ports and SEZ Ltd and Adani Transmission/Adani Energy Solutions Ltd
excluded_namesakes.reason: SEBI's September 2026 order on minimum public shareholding violations and PFUTP Regulations 3 and 4 (alleged wrongful gain of about INR 1,983.97 crore via FPI investments controlled by Vinod Adani) names these four listed Adani companies but does not name Adani Green Energy Limited - excluded as a different subject.
